title: Evaluative Suffixes: Tone, Affection and Attitude

sections.content:
You know absolute superlatives in *-ísimo* from B1 Unit 7 (*utilísimo*). Spanish also has a rich set of **evaluative suffixes** that express affection, politeness, admiration, irony or disdain—rarely physical size alone.

**Diminutives** (*-ito/-ita* everywhere; *-illo/-illa*; and *-ico/-ica* in the Caribbean, Colombia, Costa Rica and parts of Spain) add warmth, politeness or understatement: *un cafecito* (a friendly coffee), *un momentito* (just a moment), and *ahorita* (in much of Latin America, "right now" or "in a little while"). Diminutive use is noticeably higher in much of Latin America than in Spain.

**Augmentatives** (*-ón/-ona*, *-azo/-aza*) convey size, admiration (*un golazo* = a great goal) or a sudden blow (*un portazo* = a slammed door, *un codazo* = an elbow jab). **Pejoratives** (*-ucho/-ucha*, *-ejo/-eja*) express disdain or shabbiness (*un cuartucho* = a dingy little room, *un pueblucho* = a rundown little town). Context decides the exact shade: the same suffix can sound affectionate or cutting depending on tone.

sections.title: Main evaluative suffixes and what they signal
rows: Warmth, politeness or playing down: *un cafecito*, *ahorita*.
Size, admiration (*un golazo*) or a blow (*un portazo*, *un codazo*).
Disdain or poor quality: *un cuartucho*, *un pueblucho*.

items.spanish: ¿Nos tomamos un cafecito antes de volver a la oficina?
items.english: Shall we have a friendly coffee before heading back to the office?

items.spanish: Salió tan enojado que dio un portazo al cerrar la puerta.
items.english: He left so angry that he slammed the door on his way out.

items.spanish: Al principio nos dieron un cuartucho sin ventana, pero pedimos cambio.
items.english: At first they gave us a dingy little room without a window, so we asked to switch.

items.spanish: En el último minuto marcó un golazo que puso de pie a todo el estadio.
items.english: In the last minute he scored a cracker of a goal that brought the whole stadium to its feet.

sections.content: Do not translate every *-ito* as "little": *un cafecito* is not a small cup, and *ahorita* can mean "right now" or "in a minute" depending on region and tone. Stick to established derived forms rather than inventing new ones.
